blocks.etymology: Unclear. Possibly named after dentist Charles Stent. The English surname is a variant of Stein.

thesaurus.definition: a slender tube inserted inside a tubular body part (as a blood vessel) to provide support during and after surgical anastomosis

wiktionary.gloss: A slender tube inserted into a blood vessel, a ureter or the oesophagus in order to provide support and to prevent disease-induced closure.

blocks.etymology: Unclear. Possibly named after dentist Charles Stent. The English surname is a variant of Stein.

wiktionary.gloss: To insert a stent or tube into a blood vessel.

examples: My shoulder was dislocated. It was agony to have it put to rights.
I felt ill, but some fresh air and iced water set me to rights.
wiktionary.gloss: Into proper order; properly.

blocks.etymology: Borrowed from Russian токама́к (tokamák), an acronym of то(роида́льная) ка́(мера) (с) ма(гни́тными) к(ату́шками) (to(roidálʹnaja) ká(mera) (s) ma(gnítnymi) k(atúškami), “toroidal chamber with magnetic coils”).

thesaurus.definition: a doughnut-shaped chamber used in fusion research; a plasma is heated and confined in a magnetic bottle

wiktionary.gloss: A torus-shaped chamber used in nuclear fusion research in which plasma is magnetically confined.
A value that has the same value or worth for all, or almost all, people.

blocks.etymology: From Latin vermis (“a worm”) + fugare (“to drive away”), from fugere (“to flee”). See worm, and fugitive.

wiktionary.gloss: Tending to prevent, destroy, or expel worms or vermin; anthelmintic.

blocks.etymology: Compare French vitrescible.

wiktionary.gloss: That can be vitrified; vitrifiable.

examples: I ended up laughing so hard I had a little accident, so I had to waffle stomp it down the drain.
wiktionary.gloss: While showering, to step on feces to push it down the drain.
Synonym of yikes (“expressing alarm etc.”).
